# OpticQuiz

> OpticQuiz is the home of free online vision testing: a suite of fifteen honest, browser-based eye and perception tests (visual acuity, color blindness, contrast, and more), plus plain-English guides. No account, no paywall, and no ads during a test; your answers and scores are computed in your browser and never uploaded. Educational only — never a medical diagnosis — and every test states plainly what a screen can and cannot measure.

OpticQuiz is an independent, open-source project by Vince Gonzalez (source: https://github.com/zengineco/opticquiz.com). Its governing rule is honesty: stimuli are generated procedurally (canvas/SVG), scoring is transparent, and screen-calibration limits are disclosed on every page. It never claims to diagnose. A result that worries a user is framed as a reason to see a licensed optometrist or ophthalmologist, not as a verdict. Where a screen genuinely cannot do something — separate protanopia from deuteranopia, measure flicker beyond half the display refresh, or produce a glasses prescription — the test says so.

## Vision & perception tests
- [Color Vision Test](https://opticquiz.com/color/): Procedurally generated Ishihara-style "vanishing" plates. Screens red-green and blue-yellow (tritan) color deficiency, per eye. Cannot reliably separate protan from deutan.
- [Color Blindness Test for Kids](https://opticquiz.com/color/kids/): Shape-based (not number) color plates for young children (~age 3+) who can't read numbers — the child taps a hidden shape (star, heart, square). Screens red-green and blue-yellow deficiency in kids. Screening, not diagnosis.
- [Visual Acuity Test](https://opticquiz.com/acuity/): Tumbling-E chart calibrated with a credit card (85.6 mm) for true-size letters plus a viewing distance, giving an approximate Snellen result per eye. Not a refraction and not a prescription.
- [Anomaloscope](https://opticquiz.com/anomal/): Rayleigh red/green-to-yellow match, the clinical gold standard for red-green vision, approximated on a broadband screen. Suggests a protan or deutan lean; not a diagnosis.
- [Contrast Sensitivity Test](https://opticquiz.com/contrast/): Fading-letter adaptive staircase measuring the faintest contrast you can read. A relative log-CS on your (uncalibrated) screen, not a Pelli-Robson score.
- [Vernier Acuity Test](https://opticquiz.com/vernier/): Alignment hyperacuity via a two-alternative staircase; reports a sub-pixel offset threshold and an arc-second estimate.
- [Reaction Time Test](https://opticquiz.com/reaction/): Simple visual reaction time over five trials, in milliseconds. Display refresh and input lag add a small fixed offset.
- [Flicker Fusion Test](https://opticquiz.com/flicker/): Critical flicker fusion threshold in Hz, honestly capped at half the display's refresh rate (which the page detects).
- [Blind Spot Mapper](https://opticquiz.com/blindspot/): Locates and roughly sizes your eye's natural blind spot (optic disc), distance-calibrated. A demonstration, not a disease screen.
- [Dominant Eye Test](https://opticquiz.com/dominance/): Guided Miles triangle test for sighting dominance; useful for photography, archery, and shooting.
- [Farnsworth D-15](https://opticquiz.com/d15/): Color-cap arrangement test; scores total error plus the confusion axis (deutan/protan/tritan).
- [Saturation Threshold Test](https://opticquiz.com/sat/): Adaptive staircase for the faintest color you can detect versus gray, across four hue axes.
- [Hue Discrimination (Blue vs Purple)](https://opticquiz.com/hue/): Just-noticeable hue difference across seven color-neighbor pairs.
- [Amsler Grid](https://opticquiz.com/amsler/): At-home central-vision distortion check associated with macular changes (e.g. AMD). Monitoring screen, not a diagnosis.
- [Astigmatism Fan](https://opticquiz.com/astig/): Radial-line dial suggesting a possible astigmatic axis. Cannot measure a prescription.
- [Digital Eye Strain Test](https://opticquiz.com/strain/): A 15-item digital-eye-strain (computer vision syndrome) symptom self-assessment inspired by the CVS-Q, scored on-device, with evidence-based guidance. Deliberately does not blame blue light.

## Guides — direct answers to common questions
- [Am I Colorblind?](https://opticquiz.com/learn/am-i-colorblind/): The everyday signs and how to check.
- [Color Blindness in Kids: How to Test a Child](https://opticquiz.com/learn/color-blind-test-for-kids/): How to test a young child (use shapes, not numbers), the signs, what age to test, how it affects school, and what to do next.
- [Can Color Blindness Be Cured?](https://opticquiz.com/learn/can-color-blindness-be-cured/): Why inherited color blindness is permanent, and what color-boosting glasses actually do.
- [What Does a Dominant Eye Mean?](https://opticquiz.com/learn/what-does-a-dominant-eye-mean/): Eye dominance explained.
- [How to Test for Astigmatism at Home](https://opticquiz.com/learn/how-to-test-astigmatism-at-home/): The fan test and its limits.
- [What Is the Eye's Blind Spot?](https://opticquiz.com/learn/what-is-the-eye-blind-spot/): Why every eye has one and why you never notice it.
- [How Far Should You Sit From Your Screen?](https://opticquiz.com/learn/screen-distance-and-eye-strain/): Monitor distance, the 20-20-20 rule, and eye strain.
- [Why Is My Night Vision Getting Worse?](https://opticquiz.com/learn/night-vision-and-contrast/): The contrast-sensitivity connection.
- [Color Blindness, Explained](https://opticquiz.com/learn/color-blindness-explained/): Types, causes, and prevalence.
- [How Ishihara Plates Work](https://opticquiz.com/learn/how-ishihara-plates-work/): The colorimetry behind the hidden-number test.
- [What 20/20 Vision Actually Means](https://opticquiz.com/learn/visual-acuity-and-20-20/): Snellen fractions decoded.
- [Contrast Sensitivity vs. Sharpness](https://opticquiz.com/learn/contrast-sensitivity-vs-acuity/): Why 20/20 can still struggle in fog and dim light.
- [Is Blue Light Bad for Your Eyes?](https://opticquiz.com/learn/is-blue-light-bad-for-your-eyes/): The honest answer — no strong evidence screen blue light damages eyes, and blue-light glasses aren't proven to help; what really causes digital eye strain.
- [Are Online Vision Tests Worth It?](https://opticquiz.com/learn/are-online-vision-tests-worth-it/): A verified, fair comparison of the major online vision tests (ZEISS, ACUVUE, All About Vision, OneSight, personalEYES, Warby Parker, OpticQuiz) — what each does, whether it is truly free, the catch (email gates, sales funnels), and where each is genuinely the best choice.
- [How Accurate Are Online Color Blindness Tests?](https://opticquiz.com/learn/how-accurate-are-online-color-blindness-tests/): The calibration problem — why an uncalibrated consumer screen is the real limit on online color tests, what makes one trustworthy (procedural plates, randomized brightness, honest disclosure), what a result actually means, and why you can pass one site and fail another.
- [Which Color Vision Test Is Most Accurate?](https://opticquiz.com/learn/which-color-vision-test-is-most-accurate/): Plain-English comparison of Ishihara plates, the Farnsworth D-15, the anomaloscope (the clinical gold standard), and online tests — what each is for and how precise each is.

## Reference
- [Vision & Eye Test Glossary](https://opticquiz.com/learn/glossary/): Plain-English definitions of every term used across the site, each linked to its test.
- [About & Honesty Policy](https://opticquiz.com/about/): Who builds OpticQuiz and the rule that every test states what a screen can and cannot measure.
